# @applitools/task-manager

A dependency-aware task graph: you declare tasks and how they relate, and the graph decides when each one runs. Internals: [llm-docs/OVERVIEW.md](./llm-docs/OVERVIEW.md).

## Create a graph

```ts
import {makeTaskManager} from '@applitools/task-manager'

const graph = makeTaskManager()
```

## Add a task

```ts
const task = graph.add({type: 'greet', run: () => 'hello'})
await task.promise // 'hello'
```

`type` names the task in logs and queries. A task starts on its own, right after `add`.

## `deps`: read other tasks' results

```ts
const open = graph.add({type: 'open', run: async () => ({sessionId: 's1'})})
const check = graph.add({type: 'check', deps: {open}, run: ({open}) => `checked ${open.sessionId}`})
await check.promise // 'checked s1'
```

`run` gets each dependency's result by name, once it settles. A dependent still runs after a dependency fails; reading the failed one throws its error:

```ts
const failed = graph.add({type: 'open', run: () => Promise.reject(new Error('no session'))})
const close = graph.add({
  type: 'close',
  deps: {open: failed},
  run: deps => {
    try {
      return deps.open
    } catch (error) {
      return `skipped: ${(error as Error).message}`
    }
  },
})
await close.promise // 'skipped: no session'
```

## `after`: order without reading

```ts
const first = graph.add({type: 'first', run: () => 'ignored'})
const second = graph.add({type: 'second', after: [first], run: deps => Object.keys(deps).length})
await second.promise // 0 — runs after `first`, but nothing is injected
```

## Kinds: `lazy` and `dismiss`

```ts
const open = graph.add({type: 'open', kind: 'lazy', run: () => 'session'})
open.status // 'pending' — waits for a dependent
const check = graph.add({type: 'check', deps: {open}, run: ({open}) => `checked ${open}`})
await check.promise // 'checked session'

const unused = graph.add({type: 'open', kind: 'lazy', run: () => 'session'})
const close = graph.add({type: 'close', kind: 'dismiss', deps: {open: unused}, run: () => 'closed'})
await close.promise // undefined
unused.status // 'dismissed' — never ran
close.status // 'dismissed' — nothing left to close, so it doesn't run either
```

A `lazy` task runs only once a normal dependent needs it. A `dismiss` task discards the still-pending lazy tasks it rests on, and the pending tasks that rest on them. Any other task reading a dismissed dependency fails with a `DismissedError`.

## `collapse`: fuse with a successor

```ts
const check = graph.add({
  type: 'check',
  run: () => 'check',
  collapse: successor =>
    successor.type === 'close' ? {type: 'checkAndClose', run: () => 'checkAndClose'} : undefined,
})
const close = graph.add({type: 'close', deps: {check}, run: () => 'close'})
await check.promise // 'checkAndClose'
await close.promise // 'checkAndClose'
```

While a task hasn't started, it may fuse with a task added on top of it into one replacement. Both settle with the replacement's result.

## `labels`, `filter` and `keep`

```ts
const graph = makeTaskManager<{test: string}>()
const session = {}
const open = graph.add({type: 'open', labels: {test: 't1'}, keep: session, run: () => 'session'})
graph.add({type: 'check', labels: {test: 't1'}, run: () => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10))})

graph.filter(task => task.labels.test === 't1') // [open, check] — the unfinished tasks

await open.promise
graph.filter(task => task.type === 'open') // [] — settled tasks leave the graph
graph.filter(task => task.type === 'open', session) // [open] — kept while `session` is reachable
```

`labels` are free-form metadata for `filter`; the graph never reads them. `makeTaskManager<TLabels>()` types them.
